articleHeadline: Dengue surge: Can a vaccine break India's cycle?
articleSummary: Five lakh Indians hospitalised annually for dengue, with many under 12; economic toll about Rs 45,000 crore. Dengue is now an annual emergency in India, driven by urbanisation, climate change, and adaptive Aedes vectors. Dengue ranges from mild flu-like illness to severe disease with plasma leakage, respiratory distress, bleeding, or organ failure; adults risk dengue haemorrhagic fever or dengue shock syndrome, while children face higher hospitalisation and death. The virus has four serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4); infection with one offers limited protection against others. Takeda's QDenga, a tetravalent vaccine, has been recommended by a CDSCO expert panel for licencing in India; global rollout exists, with plans for local manufacturing in India. Data suggest >80% protection against dengue-related hospitalisations with sustained efficacy across serotypes, though not 100% infection protection. Caution on vaccine-induced exacerbation; a phase 4 post-marketing study is essential. Vaccination should complement vector control, urban planning, surveillance, and public awareness.

articleHeadline: Bahaya Makanan Bekas Gigitan Tikus, Bisa Sebabkan Gagal Ginjal hingga Kematian
articleSummary: As of 2026-04-01, foods contaminated by rats pose multiple serious health risks. Rats are reservoirs for pathogens, including viruses, bacteria, and fungi, and contamination can occur via urine, feces, saliva, or fur. The primary bacterial threat is leptospirosis, transmitted through rat urine, which can cause kidney failure and death. Salmonellosis from rat-associated contamination may lead to severe diarrhea, with children and older adults at highest risk. Hantavirus infection can cause severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome with high fatality. Parasitic contamination is possible from rat feces, including worm eggs or cysts. In addition, microbial toxins may be produced (enterotoxins) and remain hazardous even after the food has been heated. Caution is advised to prevent kidney injury, fatal respiratory disease, or toxin-mediated illness from rat-contaminated foods.

articleHeadline: Why tuberculosis continues to kill Filipinos
articleSummary: Philippines has the third-highest global TB burden after India and Indonesia, with incidence of at least 500 cases per 100,000 population. Globally, the World Health Organization reports 10.7 million TB infections and 1.23 million TB deaths in 2024, while treatment programs have saved over 88 million lives since 2000. In the Philippines, latent TB is common, with up to 70 percent of those infected in this category; active disease most often presents as pulmonary TB (PTB), which is contagious and causes chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, and, occasionally, hemoptysis and respiratory failure. TB can also affect lymph nodes (scrofula), brain (TB meningitis), and other organs. Stigma, crowding, and poverty contribute to transmission. Streptomycin’s discovery in the 1940s enabled TB treatment; World TB Day honors Koch’s 1882 discovery and March 24.

articleSummary: Measles, chickenpox (varicella), and conjunctivitis are highly contagious but not identical in severity. Measles is the most serious; infant vaccination with a scheduled dose provides durable immunity, greatly reducing future risk. Chickenpox vaccines exist but do not guarantee protection against all circulating varicella strains; different virus types can cause infection, though a first chickenpox episode makes reinfection unlikely. Conjunctivitis is very contagious but typically not life-threatening; spread occurs mainly through hands touching the eyes, risking household transmission. A notable outbreak occurred in 1971 during the Liberation War, spreading in refugee camps in India and in West Bengal border areas, where it was popularly known as the ‘Joy-Bangla’ disease. The article notes that conjunctivitis can recur in individuals and underscores the contagious nature of all three diseases, highlighting the importance of vaccination for measles and careful hygiene to prevent transmission.

articleSummary: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) persists in joint-associated macrophages as a viral reservoir in a murine model, according to a Nature Microbiology study published 1 April 2026. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunofluorescence microscopy, researchers found CHIKV RNA and replication intermediates in synovial and periarticular macrophages well beyond the acute phase, challenging the view of complete viral clearance after viremia resolves. Persistent infection coincided with sustained inflammatory gene expression, including cytokines and chemokines linked to arthritic pathology, implying macrophage-driven chronic chikungunya arthropathy. The findings position joint macrophages as pivotal targets for therapies aimed at eradicating reservoirs, potentially altering clinical management that currently centers on anti-inflammatory care. The study also raises the possibility that similar persistence mechanisms may apply to related alphaviruses causing protracted joint symptoms, such as Ross River or Mayaro viruses.

articleSummary: Tuberculosis remains the world's second-leading infectious killer, with about 10 million cases and over 1 million deaths annually. In Brazil, roughly 80,000 new cases are reported each year, with at least 5,500 deaths. The disease poses a markedly higher risk for patients with rheumatic diseases, especially those on immunosuppressants or biological therapies, with TB risk four to ten times higher. TB can be latent or active pulmonary disease and may trigger autoimmune or rheumatic manifestations, including bone and joint complications. Transmission is via inhalation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from people with active pulmonary TB; it is not spread by contact or objects. COVID-19 disrupted TB programs, with about 1.5 million TB deaths in 2020 per WHO. Prevention for rheumatic patients includes thorough clinical history, imaging, and TB testing before biologic therapy. Diagnosis considers persistent cough (>2–3 weeks), evening fever, night sweats, weight loss; confirmation via labs, chest imaging, and sometimes biopsy. SUS treatment lasts about six months; early diagnosis and monitoring save lives.

articleHeadline: Zika virus: symptoms and complications
articleSummary: Most people infected with Zika virus have no symptoms. When symptoms occur, illness is typically mild and short (2–7 days) and begins 3–14 days after an infected mosquito bite. Symptoms are similar to dengue or chikungunya, in areas where Zika is present, and laboratory testing is essential for correct diagnosis. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive. Zika infection is generally mild; severe disease requiring hospitalization is uncommon and the case-fatality rate is very low. In pregnancy, Zika can cause congenital brain abnormalities, including microcephaly. Zika infection is also associated with neurological conditions such as Guillain-Barré syndrome, an acute autoimmune disorder causing muscle weakness and, in 20–30% of patients, respiratory difficulty. GBS can be triggered by various infections, most commonly Campylobacter jejuni; Zika may trigger GBS, though this is very rare. Other less frequently reported neurological complications include encephalitis, meningoencephalitis, myelitis, encephalopathy, sensory neuropathy and seizures.

articleSummary: Vibrio cholerae (7PET O1) drives cholera in South Asia, with Bangladesh and North India data showing the Ganges Basin as the primary global source during the study period, challenging the notion that the Ganges Delta is the pandemic origin. In Bangladesh, V. cholerae rapidly gains and loses anti-viral defence systems against bacteriophage ICP1, creating an ongoing arms race in the human gut. articleSummary: As of 2 April 2026, Fiocruz’s InfoGripe reports influenza A cases rising nationwide, with SRAG (severe acute respiratory syndrome) activity at alert to high risk in most states across the North, Central-West, Northeast and Southeast, driven mainly by influenza A, RSV and rhinovirus. The National Influenza Vaccination Campaign began 28 March in the Northeast, Central-West, South and Southeast and runs to 30 May, with free vaccines at Basic Health Units. In the four most recent weeks (week 12, 22–28 March), SRAG positives were 27.4% influenza A, 1.5% influenza B, 17.7% RSV, 45.3% rhinovirus, 7.3% SARS-CoV-2; deaths among positives were 36.9% influenza A, 2.5% influenza B, 5.9% RSV, 30% rhinovirus, 25.6% SARS-CoV-2. Vaccination targets seniors, children, people with comorbidities, and health/education workers; pregnant women ≥28 weeks should receive the RSV vaccine. In high-SRAG states, wear high-quality masks (PFF2/N95) and practice hygiene; isolate if symptomatic. Rising SRAG activity is noted in Pará, Amapá, Mato Grosso, Distrito Federal, Maranhão, Bahia, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Espírito Santo; Paraná shows new increases; Acre, Goiás, Ceará remain alert.
notes: 記事はポルトガル語。ブラジルの保健機関Fiocruzの公式レポート（InfoGripe）に基づいており、多くの州で警戒レベルの呼吸器感染症活動が報告されている。死亡例も含まれており重症度が確認される。予防接種キャンペーンが進行中であり、政府対応は確立している。IHR基準は1つのみ該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響）。WPROスクリーニング基準は3つ該当（重症度、長期曝露、流行リスク）。現時点では対象国外への拡大報告がないため、継続監視段階が適切。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Sick-pig incident at schools reveals two schools used meat from Cuong Phat Company
articleHeadline: Vụ lợn bệnh vào trường học, lộ 2 trường dùng thịt của Công ty Cường Phát
articleSummary: Two Hanoi elementary schools were linked to pork from Cuong Phat Co amid an ASF-related meat scandal. The Hanoi Industrial Catering Company, serving about 90 schools, reports 97% of its pork is sourced from MEADELI Hanoi Nam 2 and CP Vietnam. After CP Phat’s alleged involvement, the caterer terminated all contracts with CP Phat and provided records to authorities. A preliminary review found the pork used in the two schools originated from two other slaughterhouses and was not part of the ASF-infected batch. The company is reviewing January–February 2026 imports from CP Phat. The case follows a March 17 police inspection at a centralized hog-slaughter facility in Nam Phú Commune, Hanoi, where African swine fever-infected pigs were found; eight suspects, including quarantine officers, are prosecuted for slaughtering and selling diseased meat. Parents seek clarity on which schools consumed the infected meat; the broader probe concerns nearly 300 tons of infected pork.
notes: 記事サマリーはハノイの学校給食システムへのASF感染豚肉混入事案を明示的に記載。約90校のうち2校で感染豚肉使用の可能性が指摘され、約300トンの感染豚肉流通、警察による大規模捜査、複数の刑事訴追が進行中。公衆衛生、食品安全、動物衛生の複合的リスク。

articleSummary: Avian influenza has been confirmed again in Kozhikode district, Kerala, with the outbreak centered in Kinashseri within the Kozhikode Corporation limits. Four samples were sent to Bhopal for testing, of which one tested positive. A culling operation within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre is planned today, targeting domestic poultry such as chickens and ducks. Rapid-response teams are deployed in Mankavu, Pokkun, Kinashseri, and Olavann Panchayats to carry out containment and culling in the affected zones. Authorities caution against releasing or relocating poultry in these areas. In March, infections were reported in Balussery, Kakodi, Olavann, and Perumann Panchayats within the district’s corporation boundary, indicating ongoing local transmission and the need for heightened surveillance and biosecurity."
notes: 記事は動物（家禽）での鳥インフルエンザ確認。人感染は報告されていない。3月以来、コジコード地区内で複数の村落で繰り返し検出されており、局所的な継続的伝播を示唆。発生地域にナイジェリア（Borno State）が含まれているが、記事サマリーには言及されておらず除外した。ヒト感染へのエスカレーションリスク及び地域外への拡散可能性を注視する必要がある。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Unannounced inspections of communal canteens in Hanoi and Ninh Binh after the 300-tonne diseased pork incident.
articleHeadline: Kiểm tra đột xuất bếp ăn tập thể ở Hà Nội, Ninh Bình sau vụ 300 tấn thịt lợn bệnh
articleSummary: Following the discovery of a slaughter-and-distribution network for pigs infected with African swine fever (ASF), involving 3,600 pigs and 300 tonnes of meat, Vietnam's Ministry of Health ordered 15-day unannounced inspections of dining facilities and canteens in Hanoi and Ninh Binh, starting April 1. Teams from the Ministry's Food Safety Department, the National Institute for Food Safety and Hygiene Testing, and local authorities will assess compliance with food-safety laws. The move follows police findings linking some suppliers to schools; names are not yet published. The Health Ministry warns that eating diseased pork increases disease risk and long-term health impacts, especially for children, students, and workers, and calls on provinces to intensify spot checks of dormitory/central kitchens, with parental and organizational involvement in monitoring. Experts say ASF is near 100% lethal to pigs; the virus persists in the environment, and meat from infected pigs can contain bacteria such as Salmonella.
notes: 記事サマリーではアフリカ豚熱（ASF）感染豚の流通・販売事件が中心。パラチフスと腸チフスは疾患リストに含まれているが、サマリーにおいて具体的な人間への発症報告は記載されていない。ただし、ASF感染豚肉の喫食に伴うサルモネラなどの細菌感染リスクおよび健康影響が警告されており、学校・宿舎食堂への供給が確認されている点が重大。保健省による15日間の緊急査察実施が開始されており、当局の対応能力も確認されている。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Springtime Outings: Key Diseases to Guard Against
articleHeadline: 春日踏青游玩　重点防范这些疾病
articleSummary: Published 2026-04-02, Fuzhou CDC warns spring residents to guard against Norovirus gastroenteritis, influenza, dengue fever, chikungunya, and to stay alert for animal bites, wild-plant poisoning, and pollen allergies. Norovirus remains a common fecal–oral infection; outbreaks occur in schools, daycare, and households, with symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. Prevention emphasizes hand hygiene, food safety (boiled water, fully cooked foods, washed produce, separated raw and cooked items) and surface disinfection. Influenza activity fluctuates nationally, with a rising share of influenza B but overall at a low level. April’s warmer, wetter weather boosts mosquito breeding; protect by eliminating breeding sites, changing standing water every 3–5 days, using mosquito fish where appropriate, wearing long sleeves and pants, and applying repellents. Travelers with fever after visiting risk areas should seek medical care and report travel history. Dr. Yang Jingjing of Fuzhou CDC stresses protection.
notes: 福州CDCによる季節的公衆衛生警告であり、爆発的流行や致命的な新興感染症の報告ではない。ノロウイルスはスクール・保育施設での集団発生リスク（prolonged_exposure）と高い感染性（epidemic_prone）を示す。デング・チクングニアは4月の温暖で湿った気候でのベクター活動増加に関連しており、季節的傾向として予想される。重症度や患者数の詳細記載がなく、IHR基準は該当なし。WPROスクリーニング基準2項目該当により WATCH 判定。

articleHeadlineTranslated: 300 tons of diseased pork and school meals
articleHeadline: 300 tấn thịt lợn bệnh và suất ăn học đường
articleSummary: On 2 April 2026, Hanoi authorities reported a scheme involving nearly 3,600 pigs infected with African swine fever, yielding about 300 tons of pork that entered Hanoi's meat market and the meals of public schools and kindergartens. Eight suspects have been indicted. The case reveals lapses in slaughter, quarantine, and enforcement, with over 2,900 Hanoi schools reviewing their school-meal suppliers. The incident spotlights systemic vulnerabilities rather than an absence of regulation. Experts urge digitized, end-to-end traceability: electronic tracking of each batch from farm to transport, slaughter, supplier, and school meals using lot codes; quarantine stamps to be data-accessible in real time. Proposals include a shared data platform across education, health, agriculture, and police; empowered principals to halt shipments; and transparent supplier lists, trace documents, menus, and portions for parental oversight. The aim is to prevent recurrence and restore trust.
notes: アフリカ豚熱はOIE報告対象疾病。大規模な食品安全インシデントであり、公衆衛生リスク（人への感染可能性は低いとされるが、豚肉流通を通じた拡大リスク）と規制体制の脆弱性が指摘されている。ベトナムはWPRO地域内での豚肉貿易の主要プレイヤーであるため、地域的な波及の可能性も考慮される。

articleHeadline: Kenya now Africa's deadliest mpox hotspot as outbreak spreads to 38 counties
articleSummary: Kenya is Africa's deadliest mpox hotspot with the outbreak spreading to 38 counties. Transmission occurs mainly within sexual networks, with secondary household spread and exposure across all age groups in historically endemic areas; all clades of monkeypox virus are circulating. Without rapid containment of human-to-human transmission, sustained community transmission in all settings is possible. WHO, via the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network, deployed 18 experts from Jan 1, 2025 to Mar 18, 2026 to support response in DRC, Kenya, Malawi, the Republic of the Congo, South Sudan and Uganda. Deployments cover data management and analytics, epidemiology and surveillance, laboratory services, case management, infection prevention and control, and risk communication and community engagement. WHO also supports transmission studies and vaccine safety and effectiveness research.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Thai Nguyen: Clarify the suspicion that a kindergarten fed children pork infected with cholera.
articleHeadline: Thái Nguyên: Làm rõ nghi vấn trường mầm non cho trẻ ăn thịt lợn nhiễm dịch tả
articleSummary: Thai Nguyen province, Vietnam, is investigating a food-safety incident at Hoa Binh Kindergarten, Van Lang commune, after parents reported pork used for meals tested positive for African swine fever virus (ASFV) and Escherichia coli. On 1 April, the provincial People’s Committee vice-chair directed relevant agencies to verify the information, identify responsible parties, and sanction violations, while ensuring accurate updates to parents and the public. The Department of Education will strengthen oversight of meals (boarding and canteens) to detect and rectify issues; the Department of Health will coordinate laboratory testing of related meat samples. The Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism will provide official information to the press, and the Police will monitor for violations. More than 100 parents are concerned as several children experienced digestive disturbances after meals; two samples reportedly tested positive for ASFV and E. coli. Authorities have not yet explained the pork batch quality.
notes: 記事タイトルの翻訳に誤りがある可能性（タイトルは「アフリカ豚熱」と「大腸菌」言及であり、翻訳は「コレラ菌」となっているが、サマリーから実際の病原体はASFVおよびE. coliである）。食品安全事案であるが、複数の病原体検出と子どもの健康影響の報告から公衆衛生的な関心が高い。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Sanitary Surveillance Agency bans moringa-containing supplement after a Salmonella outbreak.
articleHeadline: Vigilância Sanitária proíbe suplemento com moringa após surto de salmonela
articleSummary: As of 2 April 2026, Brazil’s Anvisa bans the sale, distribution, import, advertising, and use of the Rosabella Moringa Capsules supplement due to its association with an international Salmonella outbreak caused by an antibiotic-resistant strain. The product, manufactured by Ambrosia Brands (United States) from moringa, is linked to multiple restricted batches (5020591–5100048) though Anvisa found no official commercial imports into Brazil; online listings suggest personal-import purchases. Salmonella infection causes gastrointestinal illness with symptoms appearing 12–72 hours after ingestion, including diarrhea, fever, and abdominal cramps, lasting 4–7 days. The outbreak strain is resistant to common and alternative antibiotics, complicating severe cases requiring targeted therapy. High-risk groups include children under five, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals, with potential complications such as arterial infection, endocarditis, and arthritis. Moringa-based products have been prohibited in Brazil since 2019 due to safety concerns like possible liver damage and genotoxicity. Do not purchase or use moringa products; report irregular sales to authorities.
notes: 記事はブラジルのAnvisa（衛生監視局）によるサプリメント禁止令を主題としており、アウトブレイク菌株は抗生物質耐性を有する。発生地域にはUSAも記載されているが、記事サマリー上の主要な感染イベントはブラジルでの報告であり、同国は対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。

articleHeadline: 西班牙非洲豬瘟疫情至今已逾4個月，養豬戶損失近6.6億歐元-MoneyDJ理財網
articleSummary: As of April 2, 2026, Spain faces an African swine fever (ASF) outbreak persisting for more than four months and hammering the pork sector. Catalonia’s pork exports in January 2026 fell 17% year‑on‑year to €640 million, while nationwide losses by pig farmers totalled €657.7 million. Mercolleida notes fixed production costs per kg (feed, utilities, labor) average €1.35, and market price plunged to about €1.00/kg, pushing Catalonia losses to €170.2 million and national losses to €657.7 million; prices have recovered to €1.27/kg but remain below cost. Catalan farmers’ leader expects prices to rise above cost during May–June peak season. About 83% of global markets accept regionalization, but some buyers—Mexico, Japan, the Philippines—blocked imports, accounting for about €49.1 million of Catalonia’s 2024 exports (13%). The outbreak concentrates near Collserola hills outside Barcelona; Lleida and Girona are not yet affected. Authorities monitor wild boar movements to prevent spillover. Source: MOEA ITD.
notes: Bluedot APIが複数地域を列挙しているが、記事サマリーの主題はスペインのASF疫情。フィリピンは輸入規制国として言及されているのみ。対象国リスト内ではフィリピンのみが記事で実際に関連しているため、verified_locationsに含める。ただし、ASFは動物感染症であり、人間の感染症危機ではないため、トリアージレベルはWATCHとする。
